source.title: GigaAM: Efficient Self-Supervised Learner for Speech Recognition
source.authors: Aleksandr Kutsakov; A. Maximenko; Georgi Gospodinov; P. Bogomolov; Fyodor Minkin

record.tranche_reason: The study examines scaling effects for self-supervised speech recognition, a different modality and task from the language-model scaling claims, and reports downstream WER results.
record.gate_note: The study reports WER scaling sweeps for pretraining data and model size, but does not fit or test power laws, measure held-out cross-entropy, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its scaling findings are relevant to downstream predictability (V6), not the other versions. The WER comparisons in Table 2 concern pretraining methods and fine-tuning data amounts, not the scaling behavior captured by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper runs scaling sweeps for a self-supervised speech-recognition model (HuBERT-CTC). It varies pretraining audio (1k–100k h), model size (30M–500M) and fine-tuning data (2–2000 h), and measures downstream WER. It fits no power law and reports no held-out pretraining loss. The system is a speech encoder distilled from an ASR teacher, not a language model. So its WER sweeps do not measure what V1–V7 name. The V6 link fails on system kind, and the V5 link fails because no loss or power-law form is tested. The findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Borderline: if V6 is read as covering any pretrained model's downstream metric, the data-sweep plateau would be a limits_scope result for V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The conclusion says only that the scaling analysis confirms the approach's robustness. The stabilization above 6k hours and the 100M-vs-teacher result come from Sec 4.2, and the teacher comparison confounds pretraining method.
record.recipe_differences: This is a self-supervised speech-recognition scaling study using downstream WER, rather than a language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling-law fit. It does not fit power laws or allocate a fixed compute budget.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported WER varies with pretraining-data amount, model size, and fine-tuning-data amount. The paper describes little change above 6k hours of pretraining data and significant degradation at 1k hours.

fits_no_version.finding: For HuBERT-CTC (240M), downstream WER is nearly unchanged for pretraining audio above 6k hours and degrades significantly only at 1k hours. This holds across fine-tuning set sizes of 2–2000 h.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In teacher-distilled speech SSL, downstream ASR error saturates with unlabeled pretraining data beyond a small threshold rather than following a power law.

fits_no_version.finding: WER vs model size (30M–500M), averaged over 6k–100k h pretraining data, is shown per fine-tuning set size in a figure with no numbers stated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream ASR WER of speech SSL encoders vs parameter count.

record.problems: The scaling outcomes are reported mainly in figures without numerical point values in the text; the stated comparison between the 100M model and 240M teacher also differs in pretraining-data amount. No power-law fitting or held-out cross-entropy results are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 compares pretraining methods across fine-tuning set sizes, and Table 3 reports CR-CTC regularization effects; these do not measure the claim versions' scaling relationships. Figure 3's plotted values are represented by one row per fine-tuning-data curve rather than one row per size point.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit in parameters, data or compute.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Speech modality is studied, but no power-law form of loss is fitted or tested.
Only speech-encoder WER is measured, with no predictive fit to scale or loss, and not for language models.
No fitted exponents and no fitting choices examined.

missing.what: Pretraining-steps scaling (25k/100k/400k) is listed as a sweep, but WER vs steps is reported only as CR-CTC relative gains (Table 3), not as a scaling result.

record.verdict_notes: The study's main contribution is the GigaAM HuBERT-CTC method and Russian ASR results. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as background. All scaling evidence is figure-only except the confounded r9 comparison. The record's V6 limits_scope label is dropped because no row measures the system or measure V6 names.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss and power-law relationships in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study explores scaling in speech, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in this modality or other training regimes.
The study measures downstream WER across model and pretraining-data scales, but does not fit a predictive relationship to scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices, and departures from a fitted power law.

rows.subject: HuBERT-CTC 100M model
rows.stage_stated: pretrained, then supervised fine-tuned for ASR
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream WER of a 100M model with the 240M teacher model.

conditions.value: the 100M model used a smaller amount than the teacher; exact amount not stated

rows.note: The authors say the 100M model outperforms the 240M teacher despite using less pretraining data; this is not a controlled comparison of model size alone.
rows.check: Not a size comparison. The 240M teacher is wav2vec2-pretrained (its 4.62 WER matches the wav2vec2 row of Table 2), while the 100M model is HuBERT-CTC. Pretraining method and data differ, so this should not be a scaling row.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Pretraining-data and model-size sweeps in HuBERT-CTC speech recognition
reader_labels.reason: The text reports near-stabilization above 6k hours, degradation at 1k hours, and a 100M model outperforming a 240M teacher under differing pretraining-data conditions; these results do not establish a uniformly predictable improvement with scale (r1-r4, r9).
